# Results

## Regeneration under varying overstory retention

The thesis results provide the starting material for basal area, Douglas-fir
occurrence, and sprout-height summaries. At 10 years after harvest, redwood
regeneration was greatest in the most open treatment and declined with greater
overstory retention. Tanoak responses were comparatively modest, and
Douglas-fir regeneration was less frequent. The final figures and summaries
will retain these results only after the publication presentation and modeling
review are complete.

## Fuel conditions as reference values

Fuel conditions are reported second to support interpretation of the
silvicultural treatments and to provide reference values for subsequent fire
and fuels studies. The thesis found comparatively few treatment differences in
fine dead fuels before precommercial thinning, whereas vegetation fuels were
greater in more open treatments. The publication analysis will separate fuel
components that were previously combined and will limit treatment-comparison
emphasis to findings that aid interpretation.
